author: CNN
description:
Midterm elections are almost always bad for the president’s party. Sometimes they are very bad for the president’s party. And every so often they are historically bad. 

The first outcome seems guaranteed on Tuesday. Republicans are increasingly wary of the second. And more Democrats are daring to dream of the third. 

CNN's Audie Cornish and CNN senior political analyst Ron Brownstein discuss which eventuality is most likely based on the political climate heading into midterm elections.  

Also, Audie speaks with Cook Political Report's Jessica Taylor about seven critical toss-up Senate races and CNN's Dana Bash breaks down the midterm horse race on election eve.

2:40 Which early race calls on Tuesday could reveal a blue wave or red wall? 
5:23 The seven most critical toss-up Senate races 
11:29 CNN political director David Chalian says the midterms are a referendum on Trump 
16:52 Latino share of the Texas early vote rises
title: Midterm elections: Blue wave or red undertow?

author: CNN
description:
Democrats hold leads in five of the seven critical Senate races polled by The New York Times and Siena University as the 2026 midterm campaign comes to a close, with no clear leader in the other two races. 

Should the results of these polls match the results in Tuesday’s election, Democratic victories in the four Republican-held states where they lead outside the margin of sampling error would be enough to flip control of the Senate, if Democrats were also to hold all of their currently held seats. 

CNN's John Berman runs through the numbers at the magic wall and gets reaction from Democratic strategist Karen Finney and Republican strategist Neil Chatterjee. Also, CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten unpacks the new poling and whether Republicans are being underestimated. 

0:00 Which Senate candidates are favored in the New York Times/Sienna University poll? 
1:12 A look at how the poll results would change the Senate map if the Dem advantages hold up on election day
